neighbours.label: the verb raise / raised / raising, strongest for rearing animals, crops or children
fire: They raised sheep and goats on the hill.
Her aunt raised four children on her own.
The family made a living raising pigs.
Farmers here raise wheat and barley.
It is hard to raise a baby in a tent.
He was raising chickens behind the shop.
They raise their own vegetables every year.
My uncle raised horses for the army.
quiet: They kept sheep and goats on the hill.
Her aunt taught four children on her own.
The family made a living selling pigs.
Farmers here store wheat and barley.
It is hard to feed a baby in a tent.
He was feeding chickens behind the shop.
They buy their own vegetables every year.
My uncle sold horses for the army.

notes: My first idea was rearing as against other senses, but 'raised money' (0.45) and 'raised his hand' (0.38) fired in probes, about as much as 'raised cattle' (0.29). So this test separates the verb from other verbs, not the sense.
